messages:
Leah: Design sync notes: trying to reconcile product feedback on the autoscale edit card used in Pools list. Key asks: make burst discoverable without increasing card height, reduce cognitive load of min/max combos, and make SLO slider stateful across sessions. Link: https://intranet.redwood/figma/autoscale-card-2026 :memo:

Diego: For card, how about an affordance where min/max collapse to show a single "target" token most of the time, expanding to reveal min/max on click? That reduces noise in lists and still provides control. Target would show the effective capacity chosen by policy (could be current autoscale target).

Maya: Target token could be confusing. If we use that, hover should show the underlying min/max. Also the expand/collapse must be keyboard-friendly. Maybe add a small caret and aria-expanded.

Jun: Burst discoverability idea: show a subtle glow on the pool avatar when burst is enabled, combined with a tooltip on hover. Glow only on hover/focus to avoid noisy visuals. Clicking avatar opens the burst popover to edit policy.

Priya: SLO slider persistence: store the last selected preset per-user in local storage, but show a small "applied" chip if it's been auto-applied. Important: explicit server-side saving only when user hits save. Local storage is just UI convenience.

Leah: Good. Also product requested an inline cost delta preview next to min/max changes: tiny +$0.08/hr that updates. Keep it muted color and ensure it's visible at small sizes. We need to define currency formatting and rounding (two decimals ok).

Diego: UX microcopy: change "Min"/"Max" labels to "Minimum replicas" and "Maximum replicas" on first use with a short inline tooltip "Replicas control horizontal scaling of the pool." After user interacts once, collapse labels to Min/Max. This gives clarity without persistent verbosity.

Maya: Accessibility: when the collapse/expand of min/max occurs, we need to manage focus. If collapsed to target, hitting enter should expand and move focus into min input. Use `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded`. Also announce the change using an aria-live region.

Jun: Edge case: when burst is ON and max equals pool capacity, we need explicit messaging: "Burst enabled but pool at cap 9 There's no headroom." Maybe a red warning icon in the card to indicate user action required.

Priya: For SLO presets, we have to be careful about guardrail surprises. If a user picks "Cost-saving" and it disables burst, show a small confirmation inline: "Cost-saving will disable burst for this pool. Continue?" with a subtle undo. Don't block, just warn.

Leah: I'll update the prototype with collapsible min/max -> target mode, avatar glow for burst, inline cost delta, and first-use label expansion. Also include the save semantics note for local storage vs server save.

Diego: Dev note: will need an API endpoint to compute cost deltas (min/max changes + burst flag) and a debounce on input. Also need an event when presets are selected for telemetry.

Maya: Thanks folks 1 If no objections I'll fold these into the card PR. @Jun can you draft the warning copy for the burst at-cap case?

Jun: Will do, sending a short list of options shortly.
